programme.title: BBC Proms

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Clara Amfo presents as Chineke! Orchestra perform at the Proms alongside conductor Anthony Parnther. Features a concert of music from across four centuries and two continents, culminating in Beethoven's sunny and genial `Fourth Symphony'.

programme.title: Bob Marley Reimagined
programme.desc: Celebrate the rich legacy of reggae legend Bob Marley in a concert filmed live at Birmingham Town Hall, featuring some of his most celebrated songs and special guests including his grandson Skip Marley.

programme.title: How to Build a Cathedral
programme.desc: Architectural historian Jon Cannon goes in search of the clues that shed light on how our medieval forebears were able to build the wonders of their world. Without the technological aids of the modern world, cathedrals were built using little more than set-squares and dividers, ropes and pulleys, hammers and chisels, but were the highest buildings created since the pyramids and until the Eiffel Tower.

programme.title: Cornwall's Red River
programme.desc: Poet John Wedgwood Clarke explores the Red River in Cornwall, a watercourse barely more than a stream that has been heavily polluted by centuries of tin mining. Now, this powerful symbol of Cornish identity, home to some very rare, beautiful and resilient species, is slowly showing signs of coming back to life. Extracts from John's poem, `Red River at the A30 Culvert', reveal his mixed thoughts about the river's toxic legacy.

programme.title: Planet Earth
programme.desc: David Attenborough narrates the epic journey of a humpback whale and calf as they cross the richest seas that fringe the coasts. From tropical paradises, where the newborn calf takes his first faltering breaths, to the storm-ravaged icy polar seas, the whales' great feeding grounds, seas of great contrast and surprise are revealed.

programme.title: Da Vinci: The Lost Treasure
programme.desc: Fiona Bruce uncovers the story of Leonardo da Vinci, who is considered by many to be one of the greatest artists who ever lived. Yet his reputation rests on only a handful of pictures - including the world's most famous painting, the `Mona Lisa'. Fiona travels to Florence, Milan, Paris and Warsaw to learn more about this enigmatic genius - and to New York, where she's given a preview of a new Leonardo work.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Robert Robinson referees another duel of words and wit as Patrick Campbell, June Bolton and Richard Briers compete against Frank Muir, Joanna Lumley and Derek Jacobi.

programme.title: Face the Music

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: The team explores one of the greatest discoveries of modern astronomy that our universe is expanding, and the new questions it raises about how the cosmos works. Maggie Aderin-Pocock investigates a different cosmic speedometer.

programme.title: The Biddy Baxter Story
programme.desc: Profile of the legendary `Blue Peter' editor Biddy Baxter, with contributions from Sarah Greene, Valerie Singleton, Simon Groom and Peter Purves. Includes clips from `Blue Peter'. Presented by Sarah Dunant.

programme.title: The Riviera: A History in Pictures
programme.desc: Richard E Grant follows in the footsteps of artists who have lived, loved and painted on France's Cote d'Azur. Revealing the intertwined relationship between modern art and the development of the French Riviera as an international tourist haven, Grant explores how Impressionist painters Cezanne, Monet and Renoir first discovered the region in the 19th century when the newly-built railway arrived there.

programme.title: An Art Lovers' Guide
programme.desc: Janina Ramirez and Alastair Sooke head to Lisbon, rapidly becoming one of Europe's most popular tourist destinations. Winding through the city's cobbled streets, from its steep hills to the picturesque shoreline, the cultural riches they encounter reveal the city's fascinating history.
